title: Eighth Word The Fortunate Brothers Journey And The Talismans Opening

questions.question: What is one main difference between the intelligent brother and his brother at the beginning of the passage?
questions.answer: The intelligent brother does not suffer the same deep distress because he has good character and thinks in a positive way.

questions.question: Why does the fortunate brother move through life with more ease?
questions.answer: He understands that there is order and chooses to live according to it.

questions.question: What kind of place does he enter first on his journey?
questions.answer: He enters a garden that has both beautiful things and dirty, decaying things.

questions.question: How does he respond to the unpleasant parts of the garden?
questions.answer: He does not focus on them and gives his attention to the beneficial parts.

questions.question: What does his way of looking at the garden allow him to do?
questions.answer: It lets him benefit, rest, and continue peacefully.

questions.question: How is his reaction to the garden different from his brother’s reaction?
questions.answer: His brother focused on what was disgusting and could not settle down, but he focused on what was good and gained comfort.

questions.question: What frightening event happens to him in the desert?
questions.answer: A lion rushes toward him.

questions.question: Why is he less terrified than his brother when he sees the lion?
questions.answer: He believes the place has a ruler and thinks the lion may be acting under that ruler’s command.

questions.question: What does he do when escaping from the lion?
questions.answer: He throws himself into a deep, dry well.

questions.question: What keeps him from falling all the way down?
questions.answer: He grabs a tree growing from the side of the well.

questions.question: What does he notice about the tree’s roots?
questions.answer: Two creatures are chewing through them.

questions.question: What does he see above and below himself in the well?
questions.answer: He sees the lion above and a dragon below.

questions.question: Even though the scene is terrifying, why is his fear much lighter than his brother’s?
questions.answer: His good character leads him to good thoughts, and those thoughts help him see a hopeful side in what is happening.

questions.question: What conclusion does he reach about the strange events around him?
questions.answer: He decides they are connected and are happening by the order of a hidden ruler.

questions.question: What does he believe the hidden ruler is doing with him?
questions.answer: He believes the ruler is watching him, testing him, and directing him toward a purpose.

questions.question: What feeling grows in him after he starts wondering about the one behind the events?
questions.answer: A desire to know that ruler grows into love.

questions.question: What comes after his love for the owner of the mystery?
questions.answer: He wants to understand the mystery and develop qualities that would please its owner.

questions.question: What makes his fear disappear when he looks carefully at the fig tree?
questions.answer: He realizes it is not an ordinary tree but a sign or display pointing to many blessings prepared for guests.

questions.question: Why does he think the tree’s many kinds of fruit prove a miracle?
questions.answer: Because one tree cannot normally produce the fruits of so many different trees.

questions.question: What does he ask for after understanding that the tree points to a deeper secret?
questions.answer: He begs to be given the way to understand the mystery.

questions.question: In his prayer, how does he describe his relationship to the ruler of the place?
questions.answer: He says he is seeking refuge, sees himself as a servant, and wants to please the ruler.

questions.question: What happens right after his supplication?
questions.answer: The well opens, a doorway appears to a beautiful garden, and the threatening creatures change into helpers.

questions.question: How do the dragon and the lion change?
questions.answer: The dragon becomes like a doorway, and the lion becomes gentle and useful, even like a riding animal.

questions.question: What lesson is introduced at the end of the passage through the comparison of the two brothers?
questions.answer: The lesson is that good leads to good results, while evil leads to evil results.

questions.question: What personal quality helps the fortunate traveler remain calm compared with his brother?
questions.answer: His upright character helps him stay calmer.

questions.question: How do his thoughts affect the way the world looks to him?
questions.answer: They make things seem friendly and familiar instead of hostile.

questions.question: Why does he not struggle under the journey’s rules?
questions.answer: He accepts the order and follows it willingly.

questions.question: What mixed condition does he find in the garden?
questions.answer: He finds both enjoyable things and neglected, ugly things together.

questions.question: What wise principle does he follow in the garden?
questions.answer: He chooses to notice and use what is good instead of dwelling on what is spoiled.

questions.question: What is the result of this choice in the garden?
questions.answer: He gains benefit and rest, then continues refreshed.

questions.question: What mistake had the other brother made in a similar garden?
questions.answer: He gave too much attention to what was dirty and ended up disturbed and unable to relax.

questions.question: What danger appears in the desert after the garden?
questions.answer: A lion attacks.

questions.question: What thought gives him some comfort when he sees the lion?
questions.answer: He thinks the desert must have a master, and the lion may be under that master’s control.

questions.question: Where does he go to escape the lion?
questions.answer: He jumps into an empty well.

questions.question: What strange things does he observe while hanging in the well?
questions.answer: He sees the lion above, the dragon below, and two creatures cutting through the roots that hold the tree.

questions.question: How is his emotional response different from his brother’s in the same well?
questions.answer: He is afraid, but his fear is much less overwhelming.

questions.question: According to the passage, what is the link between good character and good thoughts?
questions.answer: Good character produces good thoughts, and good thoughts help a person notice hopeful meaning.

questions.question: What does he understand about the events in the well that his brother failed to understand?
questions.answer: He understands that they are not random and must be connected to a commanding power.

questions.question: What three things does he think the hidden ruler may be doing with him?
questions.answer: Testing him, leading him somewhere, and calling him toward a purpose.

questions.question: What feeling rises from his wish to know the hidden ruler?
questions.answer: Love rises from that wish.

questions.question: What new desire grows from that love?
questions.answer: He wants to solve the mystery.

questions.question: What moral goal grows from wanting to solve the mystery?
questions.answer: He wants to gain good qualities that would please the ruler.

questions.question: Why does the unusual fig tree become a sign of hope for him?
questions.answer: It shows him that the place is arranged intentionally and generously, not chaotically.

questions.question: What does he think the tree is showing him?
questions.answer: He thinks it is like a display or index pointing to many foods prepared for honored guests.

questions.question: What does his prayer show about his attitude?
questions.answer: It shows humility, dependence, loyalty, and a sincere wish to find and please the ruler.

questions.question: What immediate answer comes to his prayer?
questions.answer: The well opens into a peaceful garden.

questions.question: What do the dangerous creatures become after the opening appears?
questions.answer: They become obedient servants, and the lion becomes tame enough to carry him.

questions.question: What broad moral truth does the final call to compare the brothers teach?
questions.answer: It teaches that a person’s inner state and choices shape whether events lead toward goodness or misery.

questions.question: What protects him from the kind of suffering his brother faced?
questions.answer: His noble character and healthy way of thinking protect him.

questions.question: How does he view the things around him as he travels?
questions.answer: He sees them as familiar rather than threatening.

questions.question: Why is following the road easier for him?
questions.answer: He recognizes that there is a proper order and chooses to live within it.

questions.question: What two opposite kinds of things are present in the garden he enters?
questions.answer: There are attractive blessings and also rotten, unpleasant things.

questions.question: How does his attention differ from his brother’s inside the garden?
questions.answer: He pays attention to what is beneficial, while his brother had focused on what was nasty.

questions.question: After leaving the garden, where does he travel next?
questions.answer: He enters a wide desert.

questions.question: What sudden danger shocks him there?
questions.answer: He hears and sees a lion coming at him.

questions.question: What idea helps reduce his panic?
questions.answer: He thinks the lion may be under the authority of the ruler of the place.

questions.question: What action does he take to avoid the lion?
questions.answer: He jumps into a deep well.

questions.question: What object does he hold onto in the well?
questions.answer: He holds onto a tree growing from the wall.

questions.question: What shows that his situation is still serious even though he thinks well?
questions.answer: The roots are being chewed, the lion is above him, and a dragon waits below.

questions.question: Why does the passage say his fear is far less than his brother’s?
questions.answer: Because his good thoughts help him read the situation differently.

questions.question: What does he begin to believe about the strange scene?
questions.answer: He believes it is arranged by someone and is not meaningless.

questions.question: How does that belief change his sense of being alone?
questions.answer: He no longer feels abandoned, because he believes a hidden ruler sees him.

questions.question: Besides watching him, what else does he think the hidden ruler is doing?
questions.answer: He thinks the ruler is examining him and guiding him toward a destination.

questions.question: What kind of fear does he begin to experience instead of hopeless terror?
questions.answer: He feels a fear mixed with wonder and attraction.

questions.question: How does the desire to know lead to moral improvement in him?
questions.answer: Wanting to know the ruler leads to love, and that love leads him to want better character.

questions.question: What discovery about the fig tree changes everything for him?
questions.answer: He realizes the tree is a miraculous sign that points to many prepared blessings.

questions.question: Why can the tree not be explained as something ordinary?
questions.answer: Because a single fig tree cannot naturally carry the produce of countless other trees.

questions.question: What does he ask for before rescue comes?
questions.answer: He asks for help in understanding the hidden mystery and seeks protection from the ruler.

questions.question: How does the setting transform after his prayer?
questions.answer: The closed and frightening well becomes an opening to a beautiful and peaceful garden.

questions.question: What do the changes in the lion and dragon show about his new understanding?
questions.answer: They show that what seemed only dangerous can become helpful when its true meaning is understood.

questions.question: What invitation is given to the reader at the end of the passage?
questions.answer: The reader is invited to compare the two brothers and learn that good and evil lead to different outcomes.

questions.question: What kind of person is the second brother shown to be?
questions.answer: He is shown to be thoughtful, fortunate, and morally sound.

questions.question: What is the connection between his moral state and his emotions?
questions.answer: His good morals help him avoid the heavy distress that crushed his brother.

questions.question: How does he mentally approach the journey from the start?
questions.answer: He expects good and imagines matters in a hopeful way.

questions.question: What effect does this mindset have on the world around him?
questions.answer: It makes the world seem welcoming and manageable.

questions.question: Why can he travel in peace and safety?
questions.answer: He knows there is an order to follow and lives by it.

questions.question: What wise choice does he make in that garden?
questions.answer: He overlooks the corrupted parts and benefits from the wholesome parts.

questions.question: What practical benefit does he get from this choice?
questions.answer: He rests well and continues his trip strengthened.

questions.question: What lesson can be learned from the different reactions of the two brothers in the garden?
questions.answer: Two people can enter the same place but leave with very different results depending on what they focus on.

questions.question: What terrifying creature appears in the desert?
questions.answer: A lion appears and attacks.

questions.question: What belief stops his fear from becoming overwhelming?
questions.answer: He believes the lion is not acting on its own but under a ruler’s command.

questions.question: What does he do next, and where does it lead him?
questions.answer: He runs and ends up in a dry, deep well.

questions.question: What details in the well make the scene seem hopeless at first?
questions.answer: He is hanging by a tree, its roots are being chewed through, a lion is above, and a dragon is below.

questions.question: What does he conclude about the connection among all the strange events?
questions.answer: He concludes they are linked and directed by one hidden authority.

questions.question: How does this conclusion change his understanding of his own situation?
questions.answer: He sees himself not as abandoned but as part of a purposeful test.

questions.question: What two feelings combine in him as he thinks about the hidden ruler?
questions.answer: Curiosity and a gentle kind of fear combine in him.

questions.question: How does curiosity develop into a deeper spiritual response?
questions.answer: Curiosity becomes love for the one behind the mystery.

questions.question: After love appears, what are the next two steps in his inner growth?
questions.answer: He wants to understand the mystery, and then he wants to gain qualities pleasing to its owner.

questions.question: What does the many-fruited fig tree help him realize about the place he is in?
questions.answer: It helps him realize the place is carefully prepared and full of meaning.

questions.question: What explanation does he give for the tree’s impossible variety of fruit?
questions.answer: He believes a hidden ruler attached these signs to the tree by miraculous power.

questions.question: What does he ask for in his supplication?
questions.answer: He asks for refuge, shows obedience, and seeks the ruler.

questions.question: How is his prayer answered in the outer world around him?
questions.answer: The walls open, a doorway appears, and the threatening scene turns into a welcoming one.

questions.question: What new role does the lion take on after the transformation?
questions.answer: It becomes gentle and serves him like a mount.

questions.question: What moral contrast is highlighted in the closing words of the passage?
questions.answer: The contrast is that goodness brings goodness, while evil brings evil.

questions.question: Which brother in the passage experiences the road in a healthier way?
questions.answer: The fortunate and intelligent brother does.

questions.question: What inner quality shapes his experience most strongly?
questions.answer: His good morals shape it most strongly.

questions.question: How do his thoughts influence his surroundings?
questions.answer: They make his surroundings feel safe and known rather than harsh.

questions.question: Why does obeying order help him?
questions.answer: It removes unnecessary struggle and allows him to move in peace.

questions.question: What kind of garden does he encounter?
questions.answer: He encounters a place where beautiful blessings and rotten things are mixed together.

questions.question: Which part of the garden does he choose to notice?
questions.answer: He chooses the good and useful parts.

questions.question: What happens because he does not dwell on the garden’s ugly side?
questions.answer: He gains benefit and rest instead of disgust and discomfort.

questions.question: How does this compare with his brother’s earlier response to a similar place?
questions.answer: His brother became disturbed by the bad parts, but he remained balanced by focusing on the good.

questions.question: What major threat appears after he enters the desert?
questions.answer: A lion comes after him.

questions.question: What thought softens his fear?
questions.answer: He believes the lion may be carrying out the command of the ruler of that land.

questions.question: What desperate move does he make?
questions.answer: He jumps into a deep empty well.

questions.question: What keeps him suspended in the well?
questions.answer: A tree growing from the side holds him up.

questions.question: What signs of danger surround him there?
questions.answer: The roots are being cut through, a lion waits above, and a dragon threatens below.

questions.question: What does he infer from the way all the parts of the scene fit together?
questions.answer: He infers that there is a hidden ruler behind them.

questions.question: What purpose does he think may lie behind what is happening to him?
questions.answer: He thinks he may be under a test and being led somewhere meaningful.

questions.question: How does this belief affect his sense of loneliness?
questions.answer: It eases his loneliness because he feels seen and guided.

questions.question: What chain of feelings and choices follows his desire to know the hidden ruler?
questions.answer: Desire to know becomes love, love becomes a wish to solve the mystery, and that leads to wanting better character.

questions.question: What does the impossible fruit tree reveal to him?
questions.answer: It reveals that the place is arranged by extraordinary power and generosity.

questions.question: Why does he view the tree like a display prepared for guests?
questions.answer: Because it gathers signs of many foods in one place, as if introducing what has been prepared.

questions.question: What does he ask for before the rescue happens?
questions.answer: He asks for protection and seeks the ruler sincerely as a servant.

questions.question: What changes happen right after his prayer?
questions.answer: The well opens, a lovely garden appears, and the dangerous beings become servants.

questions.question: What is especially surprising about the lion’s change?
questions.answer: It becomes gentle enough to serve as a riding animal.

questions.question: What lesson are the reader and the speaker asked to learn by comparing the brothers?
questions.answer: They are asked to see that a good inner state leads to good outcomes, while a corrupt inner state leads to harmful outcomes.

questions.question: How does the passage present the second brother at the start?
questions.answer: It presents him as blessed with intelligence and good fortune.

questions.question: What is the first reason given for why he suffers less than his brother?
questions.answer: He has refined morals and hopeful thinking.

questions.question: How do these qualities change the feel of his journey?
questions.answer: They make the road seem more peaceful and less threatening.

questions.question: Why is he able to walk freely yet safely?
questions.answer: He understands and accepts the proper order instead of resisting it.

questions.question: What kind of mixed scene does he enter in the garden?
questions.answer: He enters a place filled with both attractive blessings and unpleasant decay.

questions.question: What rule guides his behavior there?
questions.answer: He follows the practice of noticing the good side of things.

questions.question: What does he gain by following that rule?
questions.answer: He benefits from the garden and gets restful relief.

questions.question: What does the contrast with his brother show about attitude?
questions.answer: It shows that attitude can turn the same place into either comfort or misery.

questions.question: What happens when he later crosses the desert?
questions.answer: A lion suddenly comes at him.

questions.question: What belief keeps him from the same level of terror his brother had?
questions.answer: He believes there is a ruler over the desert and the lion is under that ruler’s command.

questions.question: Where does he end up while escaping?
questions.answer: He ends up hanging in a deep dry well.

questions.question: What three dangers does he notice there?
questions.answer: He notices the lion above, the dragon below, and the roots being chewed through.

questions.question: What does the passage say is the reason his fear is much smaller?
questions.answer: His good morals produce good thoughts, which help him see meaning and mercy even in hardship.

questions.question: What does he realize about the strange events around him?
questions.answer: He realizes they are connected and directed, not random.

questions.question: What does he think the hidden ruler may want from him?
questions.answer: He thinks the ruler may be testing him, introducing Himself, and guiding him to a goal.

questions.question: How does fear become something more positive in him?
questions.answer: It becomes mixed with wonder and leads him to search for meaning.

questions.question: What grows out of his wish to know the one behind the mystery?
questions.answer: Love for that hidden ruler grows.

questions.question: What grows out of that love?
questions.answer: A wish to understand the mystery and become the kind of person pleasing to its owner grows.

questions.question: What causes his fear to disappear when he examines the fig tree?
questions.answer: He understands it as a miraculous sign pointing to many prepared gifts.

questions.question: Why does he reject the idea that the tree is ordinary?
questions.answer: Because one tree cannot naturally carry the fruits of countless different trees.

questions.question: What key request does he make in his supplication?
questions.answer: He asks for refuge and seeks to find and please the ruler.

questions.question: How is the answer to his prayer shown physically?
questions.answer: The well opens into a beautiful quiet garden.

questions.question: What becomes of the dragon and lion after that answer?
questions.answer: The dragon turns into an entrance, and the lion becomes a tame servant and mount.

questions.question: What final comparison is the reader invited to make?
questions.answer: The reader is invited to compare the brothers and understand that good brings good results and evil brings evil results.

questions.question: What overall message about inner character can be learned from this passage?
questions.answer: Inner character shapes how a person understands hardships and what those hardships become for him.
